title: Public sector unions call for nationwide strike on December 1

tea.why: Unions state public sector workers face significant loss of purchasing power and are dissatisfied with government salary proposals.
tea.want: Unions demand an increase in the index point, indexation to inflation, salary grid reform, and the repeal of the waiting day.
tea.changed: Nov 20: Eight public sector unions announced a nationwide strike and day of action for December 1, 2026.

summary: Eight public sector unions, including the CGT, FO, CFDT, UNSA, FSU, Solidaires, CFE-CGC, and FA-FP, have called for a nationwide strike and day of action on December 1, 2026. The unions issued a joint statement expressing dissatisfaction with the government's response to their salary concerns, specifically noting that announcements made on November 13 were insufficient. The organisations claim that public sector workers have experienced a 16% loss in purchasing power since 2017. Their demands include an increase in the index point, indexation to inflation, a restructuring of salary grids, and the removal of the unpaid waiting day for sick leave. The government is scheduled to meet with union representatives again on December 11 to discuss the budget for 2027.
response: No official response reported in the sources.
